EXAM NAME: Screening Mammography, Bilateral

REASON FOR EXAM / CLINICAL INDICATION:
Routine annual screening mammogram. Patient is asymptomatic with no new breast lumps, pain, nipple discharge, or other breast concerns. No personal history of breast cancer. Family history is negative for breast cancer in first-degree relatives.

TECHNIQUE:
Digital mammography was performed with two standard views (craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique) of each breast. Computer-aided detection (CAD) was utilized for image analysis.

COMPARISON STUDY:
Prior mammogram from 10/25/2022 (MRN EMCRAD0012345) was reviewed and used for comparison.

FINDINGS:
BREAST COMPOSITION: The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses.
RIGHT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or clustered microcalcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues appear normal. No axillary lymphadenopathy.
LEFT BREAST: No suspicious masses, architectural distortion, or clustered microcalcifications are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues appear normal. No axillary lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:
BI-RADS Category 1: Negative.
No evidence of malignancy. Comparison with prior studies shows no significant change.

RECOMMENDATION:
Routine annual screening mammogram in one year.

Electronically Signed By:
Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Radiologist

Date Signed: 10/26/2023 11:45

End of Report
